newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu makes emergency call to Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu makes emergency call to Arafat.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu appealed to Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in a phone call on Thursday to help end the clashes with Israeli troops, Israel Radio said.

It quoted Netanyahu, on a trip to Germany, as having told the PLO leader in self-ruled Gaza: "There is a need to calm the situation." It said the Israeli leader told Arafat Israel's opening of a tunnel in Jerusalem did not aim to harm Islamic sites. The violence erupted over the opening of the passage near Islam's third holiest site.

Netanyahu, who came to power 100 days ago on a promise to bolster Israeli security, decided earlier to cut short his visit to Germany by several hours on Thursday so he could return home to deal with the violence.
Palestinian health officials said at least 14 Palestinians were killed in two days of clashes with Israeli troops in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Netanyahu, leader of the right-wing Likud party opposed to swapping occupied land for peace with the Arabs, had resisted meeting Arafat, Israel's peace partner, until early this month.
